solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: I have no idea if a schemer will change

indicators.note: a schemer that will change is one whose letters get a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A puzzled person shrugs over whether a plotter will ever mend their ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if' is only a link; 'will change' shuffles the letters of A SCHEMER.
explanation.definitionFit: The colloquial reply 'search me' is a shrug meaning the speaker cannot say.

clue.text: Wild animals flanking old person from Africa

indicators.note: flanking says the shuffled animals sit on either side of the old letter
wild says the letters of animals run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: Untamed beasts surround an elderly traveller on the savannah.
explanation.definitionFit: A Somalian is a native of Somalia, in the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: A sour nude TV broadcast could be daring

indicators.note: broadcast suggests the words a sour nude TV are scattered, so rearranged

explanation.surface: Screening a grumpy naked figure on television might be considered bold.
explanation.definitionFit: Adventurous means bold and willing to take risks, synonym of daring.

clue.text: Son tucking into cooked C-rations for breakfast?

indicators.note: the son is tucked into the shuffled letters, going inside them
cooked says the letters of C-rations are prepared afresh, rearranged

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A boy wolfs down heated army field rations in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: C-rations were US army canned field meals. 'for' is a link; the question mark marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A croissant is a flaky pastry roll commonly eaten at breakfast, one example of the meal.

clue.text: Police turned over men in the French underground

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

indicators.note: turned over in a down light flips the word for men upside down

parts.note: OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Officers overturned soldiers during a raid on the Paris subway.
explanation.definitionFit: The Métro is the Paris subway railway system.

clue.text: Tickle quiet liberal with lack of awkwardness

parts.note: P is piano, the musical marking for quiet
ease is the absence of awkwardness or difficulty

explanation.surface: Someone is told to tease a quiet, open-minded person gently and without any clumsiness.
explanation.definitionFit: To tickle someone's fancy is to delight or gratify them, which is what please means.

clue.text: Royal revolutionary, one a lout might knock back

definitions.text: one a lout might knock back

indicators.note: revolutionary says the word turns round, reading backwards

parts.note: regal means royal

explanation.surface: A rebellious royal is the sort of person a yob might punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knock back' looks like a punch but means drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Lager is a beer, the drink of the stereotypical British lager lout.

clue.text: I'm surprised Scottish pine will be cut down

indicators.note: cut down says the word loses its tail end

parts.note: to ache for something is to pine for it

explanation.surface: Someone is shocked that a Caledonian pine tree is to be felled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pine' is the verb meaning to long. 'will be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ach is a Scots exclamation of surprise or annoyance.

clue.text: Come in and get involved in record

definitions.meaning: to ... a contest or field is to get involved in it
to ... data is to record it

explanation.surface: An instruction to step inside and help make a record.
explanation.definitionFit: Enter covers coming into a place, taking part in something, and writing details into a log.

clue.text: Old joke involving Carlsen super-fan I've been told?

indicators.note: being told is hearing it, so the words are said aloud

parts.note: Magnus Carlsen is a chess world champion, so his devotee is a chess nut

explanation.surface: An old gag about a devoted follower of a chess grandmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A chestnut is a stale, oft-repeated joke or story.

clue.text: Leave home and travel abroad

parts.note: to move is to travel from place to place
out means away from home, abroad

explanation.surface: A young person quits the family house and heads off overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving out means relocating from a residence, especially a young adult quitting the parental house.

clue.text: What can be part of a drum kit and a stovepipe?

definitions.text: What can be part of a drum kit
definitions.meaning: a pair of cymbals worked by a pedal, usually spelt hi-hat

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what links a percussion set-up with a chimney flue.
explanation.definitionFit: A drummer's pedal cymbals share the name; a stovepipe is a tall formal hat, literally a high one.

clue.text: Remote possibilities of awfully hot snogs around lake

parts.note: around means in the vicinity of, so this is L, the map abbreviation for lake, set next to the shuffled words

indicators.note: awfully says the words hot snogs are put together badly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Steamy kisses by a lakeside are, it seems, unlikely to happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' shuffles HOT SNOGS into ONGSHOTS. 'around' tempts a container, but means 'in the vicinity of': L simply stands beside the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Long shots are bets or attempts with little chance of success, so unlikely outcomes.

clue.text: Bishop seen around a church in sporty motor

indicators.note: the bishop's letters are seen around the next pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: RR is Right Reverend, the title of a bishop
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A clergyman is spotted, with his congregation, behind the wheel of a fast car.
explanation.definitionFit: A racer is a car built for speed or competition, a sporty motor.

clue.text: He declared a drunk sober

indicators.note: drunk says the words he declared a are scrambled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A man insists a tipsy friend is actually stone cold sober.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear-headed means thinking clearly and not intoxicated, so sober.

clue.text: Island that can be spotted in Tokomaru Bay

indicators.note: something spotted in a phrase is found sitting inside its letters

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A clue pretending a Caribbean island might be glimpsed from a bay in New Zealand.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Island that can be' as the definition; the definition is just 'Island', and 'that can be spotted in' is the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Aruba is a Dutch Caribbean island off the coast of Venezuela.

clue.text: Grand way to stop feeling of antagonism in criminal

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand

indicators.note: the way is put in to stop up the feeling, sitting inside it

parts.note: anger is a hostile feeling
ST is street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone seeks a fine way to calm their hostility toward a lawbreaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangster is a member of a gang of violent criminals.

clue.text: Good girl and I picked up part of a socket set?

parts.note: a lass is a girl

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: the pronoun I

explanation.surface: Two people collect a component of a mechanic's spanner kit.
explanation.walkthrough: A socket set is a toolkit, but here the socket is an eye socket.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass eye is an artificial eye, set in the eye socket.

clue.text: Spartans fighting around top of damaged bunkers

indicators.note: the shuffled Spartans sit around the next letter
fighting says the Spartans are in disarray, their letters rearranged
top of in a down light picks the first letter of damaged

explanation.surface: Greek warriors battle around their wrecked shelters.
explanation.walkthrough: Bunkers poses as military shelters but is the golf sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Sand traps is the American golfing term for bunkers.

clue.text: Criminal and inmate missing first right around Ohio

indicators.note: the shortened word goes around the state abbreviation
missing first says the earliest occurrence of the right abbreviation is dropped

parts.note: a prisoner is an inmate
O is an abbreviation for the US state of Ohio

explanation.surface: A lawbreaker and a convict are both on the loose somewhere near Ohio.
explanation.definitionFit: A poisoner is a criminal who kills or harms with poison.

clue.text: Pamphlet found on conservative shrink

indicators.note: in a down-style reading the pamphlet comes after, placed on the conservative piece

parts.note: a tract is a short pamphlet, often religious

explanation.surface: A leaflet has turned up belonging to a right-wing psychiatrist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shrink' poses as a psychiatrist but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To contract is to get smaller or draw together, the same as to shrink.

clue.text: Drug smuggler sprinted back to meet firm

indicators.note: back says the word for sprinted runs backwards

parts.note: ran is a synonym for sprinted
CO is company, a firm

explanation.surface: Someone dashed back to keep an appointment with a business.
explanation.definitionFit: Narco is informal, chiefly American, slang for a drug trafficker.

clue.text: Layers which can be seen in some diamonds?

definitions.meaning: the bottom layers or foundations of something

definitions.text: which can be seen in some diamonds?
definitions.meaning: a baseball diamond has ... at its corners

explanation.surface: A jeweller describes strata visible inside certain gems.
explanation.walkthrough: The diamonds are baseball fields, not gems.
explanation.definitionFit: A base is the lowest layer; a baseball infield, the diamond, has four bases.

clue.text: Composer getting hold of ecstasy in The Strand?

indicators.note: the composer gets hold of the next letter, holding it inside

parts.note: J S Bach, the composer
E is the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A composer takes drugs on a famous London street.
explanation.walkthrough: The Strand is a London street; a strand is also a shore. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Strand is an old or poetic word for a shore or beach.

clue.text: Wise man skirting Republican military type

indicators.note: skirting says the wise man goes round the edges of the next letter

parts.note: a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: A thoughtful person avoids a right-wing soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarge is informal for sergeant, a non-commissioned army officer.

clue.text: What one will do changing to an automatic car … idle?

definitions.text: What one will do changing to an automatic car
definitions.meaning: with automatic gears, one will shift gear less often

explanation.surface: A driver switching to an automatic wonders what will happen, then just sits there.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiftless describes someone lazy and lacking drive; read as two words, an automatic means shifting less.

clue.text: Vision wizard gets after first of incantations

indicators.note: the wizard gets after, coming behind, the other piece
first of picks out the opening letter of incantations

parts.note: a mage is a wizard

explanation.surface: A sorcerer has a vision after beginning his spells.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a picture in the mind, a vision.

clue.text: Place some might park their butts for a while?

definitions.text: Place some might park their butts for a while?

parts.words: Place some might park their butts for a while?
parts.note: butts reads as backsides being sat down, but means cigarette ends

explanation.surface: Somewhere people might sit down for a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: Butts are cigarette ends, not bottoms.
explanation.definitionFit: Smokers rest or stub out their cigarette ends in this dish.

clue.text: Have an aversion to energy-sapped bowler?

indicators.note: energy-sapped says E, the physics symbol for energy, is drained out of the word

parts.note: to hate something is to have an aversion to it

explanation.surface: A tired cricketer dislikes bowling.
explanation.walkthrough: The bowler is the hat, not a cricketer; the question mark marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowler is a type of hard round felt hat, one example of headwear.

clue.text: A group performing in desert

parts.note: a band is a musical group
on means on stage, performing

explanation.surface: A musical group playing out in an arid wilderness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' is the verb, not the sandy place.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon someone is to leave them in the lurch, to desert them.

clue.text: Hard type seen at The Den is more fiery than others

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
an otter is a creature that lives in a riverside den

explanation.surface: A tough character at Millwall's ground is the most hot-headed of the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: The Den is the London ground of Millwall football club, but here a den is an animal lair, an otter's home.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotter is the comparative of hot, which can mean spicy or fiery.

clue.text: Famous player upset bar in month in France once

parts.note: Lionel Messi is a famous footballer

indicators.note: upset in a down light turns the word for bar over, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a rod is a bar

explanation.surface: A star footballer is upset by a pub during a month spent in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Messidor was the tenth month of the French Republican calendar, used after the Revolution.
